t.4.38.1: Rāma, the foremost of those who uphold dharma, embraced with both arms Sugrīva, who stood with joined palms speaking thus, and replied to him.
t.4.38.2: That Indra pours down rain upon the earth would be no wonder, nor that the thousand-rayed Āditya should make the sky free of darkness.
t.4.38.4: It would be no wonder, gentle one, that what is noble should be found thus in you. I know you, Sugrīva, to be one who always speaks kindly.
t.4.38.3: O gentle one, the moon with its rays may make the earth spotless; and likewise, O scorcher of foes, only one such as you could repay the kindness of friends.
t.4.38.5: With you as my protector, friend, I shall conquer all my enemies in battle. You alone are my true-hearted friend and ally; you should give me your help.
t.4.38.6: The vilest of rākṣasas carried off Vaidehī through deceit, to his own destruction, just as Anuhlāda carried off Śacī Paulomī.
t.4.38.7: Before long I shall slay that Rāvaṇa with sharpened arrows, just as Śatakratu, the slayer of foes, slew the arrogant father of Paulomī.
t.4.38.8: And just at that moment a cloud of dust rose up, covering in the sky the hot and fierce radiance of the thousand-rayed sun.
t.4.38.9: The quarters were thrown into confusion, overwhelmed by that dust, and the whole earth, with its mountains, woods and forests, trembled.
t.4.38.10: Then the entire earth was covered by countless monkeys, resembling lords of mountains, sharp-fanged and of mighty strength.
t.4.38.11: Then, within the mere interval of a blink, the earth was covered by those leaders of the monkey troops, who could take any form at will and were each attended by retinues numbering hundreds of crores.
t.4.38.13: And by monkeys the colour of the rising sun, and by monkeys pale as the moon, and by others the colour of lotus filaments, and by white ones who had made their dwelling on Meru.
t.4.38.12: With mighty monkeys dwelling by the rivers, in the mountains and by the sea, roaring like thunderclouds, and with others that roam the forests,
t.4.38.14: Then the glorious and heroic monkey named Śatabali appeared, surrounded by ten thousand koṭis.
t.4.38.15: Then the mighty father of Tārā, gleaming like a golden mountain, appeared, accompanied by many tens of thousands of crores.
t.4.38.16: Resembling the filaments of a lotus, his face shining like the rising sun, he was wise, the foremost of monkeys, the very best among all the monkeys.
t.4.38.17: Then the glorious Kesarī, father of Hanumān, was seen, accompanied by many thousands of troops of vānaras.
t.4.38.18: Gavākṣa, the great king of the Golāṅgūlas, of fearsome valour, was seen surrounded by a thousand crores of monkeys.
t.4.38.19: Dhūmra, the destroyer of enemies, came forward, surrounded by two thousand koṭis of bears of terrible speed.
t.4.38.20: The troop-leader named Panasa, of mighty valour, arrived surrounded by three crores of fearsome monkeys resembling great mountains.
t.4.38.21: Then the troop-leader named Nīla, huge of body, his form like a heap of dark collyrium, was seen, surrounded by ten crores of monkeys.
t.4.38.22: Then the mighty troop-leader Darīmukha also came, surrounded by a thousand koṭis, and presented himself before Sugrīva.
t.4.38.23: Mainda and Dvivida, both mighty sons of the Aśvins, were seen with a thousand crores of crores of vānaras.
t.4.38.24: Then Gandhamādana arrived, followed from behind by monkeys numbering a thousand and a hundred of thousands of crores.
t.4.38.26: Then Tāra, the monkey of fearsome valour, radiant as a star, was seen from afar with five crores of monkeys.
t.4.38.25: Then the crown prince Aṅgada, whose valor equaled his father's, arrived, surrounded by a thousand padmas and a hundred śaṅkus.
t.4.38.27: The heroic monkey Indrajānu, a leader of troops, came into view, lord of eleven crores and surrounded by them.
t.4.38.28: Then Rambha arrived, resembling the newly risen sun, surrounded by ten thousand, by a thousand, and by a hundred as well.
t.4.38.29: Then the heroic troop-leader, the mighty monkey named Durmukha, appeared, surrounded by two crores of monkeys.
t.4.38.30: Hanumān was seen surrounded by a thousand koṭis of monkeys of terrible valour, resembling the peaks of Kailāsa.
t.4.38.31: And Nala too, of great valour, arrived, surrounded by tree-dwellers numbering a hundred crores, a thousand and a hundred.
t.4.38.33: Covering the whole earth, the mountains and the forests, the monkeys, leaping up and bounding along and roaring, advanced toward Sugrīva like masses of clouds toward the sun.
t.4.38.32: Śarabha, Kumuda, Vahni, and the monkey Rambha as well: these and many other monkeys, able to take on any form at will.
t.4.38.34: Raising a great many cries, the mighty ones, overjoyed, bowed their heads and announced themselves to Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys.
t.4.38.36: Sugrīva, knower of dharma, having swiftly presented all those bulls among the vānaras to Rāma, stood with joined palms and spoke.
t.4.38.35: Other foremost vānaras, having assembled as was fitting and having come together with Sugrīva, then stood with joined palms.
t.4.38.37: O lords of the monkeys, having duly stationed the troops at ease among the mountain cascades and in all the forests, one who understands forces is able to take full measure of the army.
